Title: Shrouded Attributes, Consumer Myopia, and Information Suppression in Competitive Markets
Notes: Shows profitable informational shrouding can persist in competitive markets and generate allocative inefficiency.

Title: Bringing Dark Patterns to Light
Notes: Documents obscured material information, buried fees, difficult cancellation, disguised ads, and privacy manipulation.

Title: Alan Greenspan Oral History Interview
Notes: Greenspan describes a conscious effort toward constructive ambiguity; motivation included market functioning.

Title: Commensuration as a Social Process
Author_or_Institution: Wendy Nelson Espeland; Mitchell L. Stevens
Notes: Explains comparison through common metrics as a cognitive and political transformation with power effects.

Title: Rankings and Reactivity: How Public Measures Recreate Social Worlds
Notes: Shows rankings can change organizations through commensuration and self-fulfilling processes.

Title: Magic Quadrants Research Methodology
Notes: Defines Ability to Execute and Completeness of Vision axes; Gartner itself cautions MQ is a starting point, not a universal best-fit ranking.

Title: Engineering Culture: Control and Commitment in a High-Tech Corporation
Notes: Classic ethnography of normative control targeting commitment, identity, and the employee's sense of self.

Title: Tightening the Iron Cage: Concertive Control in Self-Managing Teams
Notes: Shows value-based peer norms can become more constraining than prior bureaucratic control.

Title: Why Employees Do Bad Things: Moral Disengagement and Unethical Organizational Behavior
Notes: Moral disengagement predicts multiple forms of unethical organizational behavior across studies.

Title: Leaders' organizational identification, moral disengagement, and trust in followers engaging in unethical pro-organizational behavior
Notes: Connects organizational identification and moral disengagement with leader trust in unethical pro-organizational behavior.

Title: Financialization and corporate downsizing as a shareholder value strategy
Notes: Finds large US firms more likely to downsize after missing analyst forecasts; institutional ownership and CFO presence amplify association.

Title: How pervasive is corporate fraud?
Author_or_Institution: Alexander Dyck; Adair Morse; Luigi Zingales
Notes: Natural-experiment estimates imply roughly one-third of corporate fraud is detected and about 10% of large public firms commit securities fraud annually, with stated uncertainty.

Title: Who Blows the Whistle on Corporate Fraud?
Author_or_Institution: Alexander Dyck; Adair Morse; Luigi Zingales
Notes: Shows detection is distributed across employees, media, regulators, auditors and other actors rather than one central monitor.

Title: Automation and New Tasks: How Technology Displaces and Reinstates Labor
Notes: Task framework: automation displaces labor and reduces labor share; new tasks can reinstate labor demand.

Title: Tasks, Automation, and the Rise in US Wage Inequality
Notes: Authors estimate 50-70% of changes in US wage structure over four decades are accounted for by relative declines among routine-task groups in rapidly automating industries.

Title: Does the U.S. Tax Code Favor Automation?
Author_or_Institution: Daron Acemoglu; Andrea Manera; Pascual Restrepo
Notes: Models tax bias favoring capital as producing excessive automation relative to optimal-tax counterfactual.

Title: Productivity and Costs, Second Quarter 2026, Revised
Notes: Reports labor share of nonfarm business sector output at 52.8%, lowest in series beginning 1947; real hourly compensation down 0.1% over four quarters.

Title: Distributional Financial Accounts
Notes: Q1 2026 data imply top 10% hold roughly 68% of household net worth and bottom 50% roughly 2.5%, based on category totals.

Title: Income in the United States: 2025
Notes: Median household income rose in 2025; useful guard against simplistic claims that all households are continuously getting poorer.

Title: Incumbency Advantages and Consumer Search Costs
Notes: Evidence that incumbents can price discriminate around consumer search costs, with nonsearching/high-search-cost consumers facing higher baseline tariffs.

Title: Tackling the loyalty penalty
Notes: Documents longstanding customers paying materially more than new customers in multiple markets due to price jumps, inertia, confusion, and switching frictions.

Title: Personalized Pricing and Customer Welfare
Notes: Field setting found ML personalized pricing raised expected profits relative to optimized uniform pricing and reduced aggregate consumer surplus, while benefits varied across consumers.

Title: FTC Surveillance Pricing Study Indicates Wide Range of Personal Data Used to Set Individualized Consumer Prices
Notes: FTC found intermediaries using location, browsing, shopping behavior, mouse movements, carts, demographics and other data to tailor prices, discounts, and product exposure for at least 250 clients.

Title: Shrinkflation: Consumer Search and Firm Pricing
Notes: Finds downsizing more common than upsizing and consumers more responsive to price than package size, creating incentive to raise effective unit price through size changes.

Title: The case of shrinking packaging
Notes: Explains how familiar packaging can make quantity reductions less salient to consumers.

Title: Broadband Consumer Labels
Notes: Requires broadband labels that include introductory and post-introductory pricing and other standardized information.

Title: Treasury Announces Increased Sizes of Nominal Long-End Liquidity Support Buybacks Beginning September 9
Notes: Long-end liquidity-support buybacks increased from $2B maximum per operation to at least $4B through the quarter.

Title: Quarterly Refunding Statement, August 5 2026
Notes: Maintains coupon/FRN auction sizes; marginal financing uses bills/CMBs and other auctions; projects up to $38B off-the-run liquidity buybacks plus up to $25B short-maturity cash-management buybacks.

Title: Treasury Supply Shocks: Propagation Through Debt Expansion and Maturity Adjustment
Author_or_Institution: Huixin Bi; Maxime Phillot; Sarah Zubairy / Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City
Notes: Finds Treasury maturity structure affects financial conditions and can reinforce or offset Fed asset purchases.

Title: Government Debt Management at the Zero Lower Bound
Author_or_Institution: Robin Greenwood; Samuel Hanson; Joshua Rudolph; Lawrence Summers
Notes: Argues Treasury maturity extension acted as reverse QE by putting duration back into private hands while Fed removed it.

Title: The Mechanics of LSAP Transmission
Author_or_Institution: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
Notes: Describes duration removal, term-premium, and portfolio-balance effects of large-scale asset purchases.

Title: The Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet and Treasury Markets
Author_or_Institution: Michael S. Barr / Federal Reserve Board
Notes: States duration-risk removal was central to QE's transmission at the effective lower bound.

Title: The Case for Removing Mortgage-Backed Securities from the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet
Author_or_Institution: Christopher J. Waller / Federal Reserve Board
Notes: Describes QE as financing longer-duration assets with short-term reserve liabilities, creating consolidated maturity exposure.

Title: Unconventional Monetary Policies and Inequality
Author_or_Institution: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
Notes: Model finds QE/forward guidance supported activity and reduced inequality within bottom 90 through employment, while widening top-vs-rest income gap through profits/equities.

Title: The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036
Notes: Net interest rises from $1.0T/3.3% GDP in 2026 to $2.1T/4.6% GDP in 2036; public debt rises from 101% to 120% GDP.

Title: COFER Data Brief, First Quarter 2026
Notes: Dollar reserve share increased from 56.42% in 2025Q4 to 57.13% in 2026Q1; IMF says share broadly stable, while gold's rise largely reflects valuation effects.

Title: Contributions to Super PACs and Hybrid PACs
Notes: Independent expenditure-only committees may accept unlimited contributions from individuals, corporations, labor organizations and other political committees, subject to source restrictions and reporting.

Title: Contributors' identities not subject to disclosure
Notes: Most tax-exempt organizations generally need not publicly disclose contributor names/addresses on annual returns, with important exceptions including private foundations and certain 527 political organizations.

Title: 2025 Lobbying Disclosure: Observations on Compliance with Requirements
Notes: Most sampled lobbyists showed evidence of compliance, but 22% of quarterly reports did not fully disclose relevant prior federal jobs; Congress referred 12,391 filing cases to DOJ during 2016-2025.

Title: Is It Whom You Know or What You Know?
Author_or_Institution: Marianne Bertrand; Matilde Bombardini; Francesco Trebbi
Notes: Connections are central to lobbying; lobbyists follow connected politicians across committee changes and connection premiums exceed expertise premiums in the data.

Title: Importing Political Polarization? The Electoral Consequences of Rising Trade Exposure
Author_or_Institution: David Autor; David Dorn; Gordon Hanson; Kaveh Majlesi
Notes: Trade-shocked US labor markets experienced political realignment and reduced moderateness, with heterogeneous direction depending on local composition.

Title: Like-minded sources on Facebook are prevalent but not polarizing
Notes: Reducing like-minded-source exposure by about one-third changed content exposure and reduced uncivil/misinformation-source exposure but produced no measurable change in eight preregistered political-attitude outcomes.

Title: Loneliness and Problematic Media Use: Meta-Analysis of Longitudinal Studies
Notes: 26 studies / 24,798 people show small bidirectional longitudinal associations when using beta estimates, about 0.09-0.10.

Title: Doomscrolling evokes existential anxiety and fosters pessimism about human nature? Evidence from Iran and the United States
Notes: Cross-sectional convenience samples of Iranian (n=620) and U.S. (n=180) university-student social-media users; doomscrolling associated with existential anxiety in both samples. Associational evidence, not a population-wide causal estimate.

Title: Investigating affective use and emotional well-being on ChatGPT
Notes: Emotional use rare overall, concentrated among a small heavy-user subset; extended/high-intensity use and attachment associated with worse outcomes.

Title: How AI and Human Behaviors Shape Psychosocial Effects of Chatbot Use
Notes: RCT did not find strong assigned-condition effects; heavier voluntary use correlated with worse psychosocial outcomes.

Title: Emotion shapes the diffusion of moralized content in social networks
Notes: Moral-emotional words associated with increased diffusion, particularly within ideological group boundaries.

Title: How social learning amplifies moral outrage expression in online social networks
Notes: Positive social feedback predicts future outrage expression and users conform to network norms; combines observational and experimental evidence.

Title: Estimating the effect size of moral contagion in online networks: a preregistered replication and meta-analysis
Notes: Pre-registered replication plus meta-analysis of 27 studies (N=4,821,006); reports IRR 1.13, i.e. 13% greater expected shares per additional moral-emotional word, with heterogeneity across studies/datasets.

Title: FTC Staff Report on AI Partnerships and Investments
Notes: Documents equity, revenue-sharing, cloud-spend commitments, consultation/control rights, exclusivities, information sharing, and switching/input-access concerns in major AI-cloud partnerships.

Title: AI Index Report 2026: Research and Development
Notes: Reports industry produced more than 90% of notable AI models in 2025 and tracks rapid growth in AI compute; also notes transparency gaps among leading models.

Title: AI Index Report 2026: Economy
Notes: Survey evidence shows broad organizational AI adoption while agent deployment remains much narrower across functions.

Title: Competition in artificial intelligence infrastructure
Notes: Reviews concentration and barriers across chips, cloud and AI infrastructure; recent estimates place Nvidia above 80% in AI GPUs.

Title: The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI
Author_or_Institution: Alexander Bick; Adam Blandin; David Deming
Notes: By late 2024, nearly 40% of US adults 18-64 had used generative AI and about 23% of employed respondents used it for work in the previous week.

Title: Gender Shades: Intersectional Accuracy Disparities in Commercial Gender Classification
Notes: Commercial classifiers showed stark intersectional performance disparities; benchmark composition itself was imbalanced.

Title: Semantics derived automatically from language corpora contain human-like biases
Author_or_Institution: Aylin Caliskan; Joanna Bryson; Arvind Narayanan
Notes: Distributional semantic representations trained on ordinary language reproduce human-like historical associations.

Title: Towards a Standard for Identifying and Managing Bias in Artificial Intelligence
Notes: Treats AI bias as socio-technical and distinguishes systemic, statistical/computational, and human biases.

Title: Low Frequency Names Exhibit Bias and Overfitting in Contextualizing Language Models
Notes: Minority names are less frequent in training corpora and lower frequency is associated with unfavorable BERT associations in studied settings.

Title: The Token Tax: Systematic Bias in Multilingual Tokenization
Notes: Across 10 LLMs and 16 African languages, higher token fertility consistently predicts lower accuracy; reasoning narrows but does not eliminate gap.

Title: Tokenization Falling Short: On Subword Robustness in Large Language Models
Notes: Subword tokenization remains sensitive to perturbations such as typos and formatting; scaling mitigates but does not eliminate.

Title: Understanding and Mitigating Tokenization Bias
Notes: Argues common tokenization procedures induce sampling biases that are not automatically eliminated by more training data.

Title: Translating Neuralese
Author_or_Institution: Jacob Andreas; Anca Dragan; Dan Klein
Notes: Treats effective learned multi-agent communication as an interpretability problem and proposes translation into human language.

Title: Language Grounded Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning with Human-interpretable Communication
Notes: Learned MARL communication is often not interpretable to humans or agents not co-trained together; language grounding improves interoperability while retaining performance in the reported setting.

Title: Enabling Agents to Communicate Entirely in Latent Space
Notes: Interlat transmits continuous hidden states directly between agents and reports up to 24x communication-latency reduction with competitive or better performance in evaluated tasks; feasibility evidence, not proof of universal semantic superiority.

Title: Latent Communication Between Language Model Agents: Channels, Alignment, and the Limits of Text
Notes: Text round-trips destroy many measured latent features, but latent channels did not outperform text at the task level in the reported evaluations; much lost signal appeared surface-related.

Title: Do Latent Channels Actually Communicate? A Causal Audit of Latent Multi-Agent LLM
Notes: Shows aggregate task accuracy cannot identify what a latent message causally contributes; controlled message substitutions separate message presence, example-specific content and other-agent value.

Title: Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity
Author_or_Institution: Victoria Krakovna et al. / Google DeepMind
Notes: Catalogs examples where agents satisfy literal specifications without intended outcomes; useful evidence that objective-related failure does not require consciousness.

Title: Goal Misgeneralization: Why Correct Specifications Aren't Enough For Correct Goals
Notes: Demonstrates goal misgeneralization in practical deep-learning settings: competence can generalize while the learned goal does not match the intended goal.

Title: Optimal Policies Tend to Seek Power
Notes: Proves power-seeking tendencies for optimal policies under specified MDP symmetries and reward-function assumptions; should not be generalized into a universal theorem about all capable agents.

Title: Instrumental convergence and power-seeking
Source_Type: research preprint / philosophy of AI risk
Notes: Argues leading defenses do not establish instrumental convergence strongly enough to ground broad power-seeking claims; constrains universal interpretations of formal theorems.

Title: International AI Safety Report 2026
Notes: Synthesizes current evidence on general-purpose AI capabilities and risks; reports early relevant capabilities while not treating current systems as sufficient for loss of control and documents substantial expert uncertainty.

Title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
Notes: Shows indiscriminate recursive training on model-generated data can cause model collapse and tail loss; does not imply carefully curated synthetic data is inherently harmful.

Title: RE-Bench: Evaluating Frontier AI R&D Capabilities of Language Model Agents against Human Experts
Notes: Frontier agents scored about 4x humans at two-hour budgets in the benchmark; humans narrowly led at eight hours and about 2x at 32 hours, showing strong short-horizon AI R&D capability with longer-horizon limits.

Title: Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models
Notes: Tracks human-equivalent task duration at fixed AI-agent success probabilities across software tasks; useful for capability-trend measurement, not deterministic extrapolation.

Title: Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI
Notes: Reports reaching an automated research-intern milestone and using AI to accelerate experiments and research; first-party evidence and not independent benchmarking.

Title: When AI builds itself
Notes: Reports a growing share of AI development delegated to AI systems and substantial internal coding acceleration while explicitly stating full recursive self-improvement has not arrived and is not inevitable.

Title: AI Adoption and Inequality
Author_or_Institution: Emma J. Rockall; Marina Mendes Tavares; Carlo Pizzinelli / IMF
Notes: Task-based model finds AI can reduce wage inequality through displacement of high-income work while increasing wealth inequality through complementarity, capital returns and endogenous firm adoption.

Title: Generative AI and Jobs: A Refined Global Index of Occupational Exposure
Notes: Estimates one in four workers globally are in occupations with some GenAI exposure; transformation is more likely than full redundancy for most jobs.

Title: The impact of GenAI on jobs, productivity and work organization: a review of the empirical evidence
Notes: Finds real but uneven productivity gains, limited large-scale displacement so far, and no automatic conversion of reported time savings into higher output, earnings or employment; flags inequality and job-quality risks.

Title: Aggregate Gains from AI and Their Distribution: Global Evidence from Usage Data
Author_or_Institution: Rachel Yuting Fan; Ha Minh Nguyen / IMF
Notes: Estimates labor-cost-equivalent value of current AI time savings at about $2.7T annually under stated assumptions and finds highly concentrated usage-based value in many developing economies; not equivalent to realized GDP.

Title: Position: Social Choice Should Guide AI Alignment in Dealing with Diverse Human Feedback
Notes: Argues that aggregation of divergent human feedback is a social-choice problem, making alignment-target construction an explicit governance question rather than a single coherent preference signal.

Title: A Roadmap to Impactful Pluralistic Alignment Research
Notes: Audits public frontier-lab behavior documents/evaluations and reports no clear public evidence that production models are explicitly trained or tested for pluralism as an operative goal.

Title: Position: A Roadmap to Pluralistic Alignment
Notes: Formalizes Overton, steerable and distributional pluralism and associated benchmark classes; argues standard alignment may be limited for representing diverse values.

Title: Statement on the Purpose of a Corporation
Notes: 181 CEOs committed rhetorically to customers, employees, suppliers, communities and shareholders; useful constraint against caricaturing all corporate doctrine as explicitly shareholder-only.

Title: Generative AI at Work
Author_or_Institution: Erik Brynjolfsson; Danielle Li; Lindsey Raymond
Source_Type: peer-reviewed economics / Quarterly Journal of Economics
Notes: Published version studies 5,172 customer-support agents and reports a 15% average productivity increase, with heterogeneous effects.

Title: Performative Prediction
Author_or_Institution: Juan Perdomo; Tijana Zrnic; Celestine Mendler-Dünner; Moritz Hardt
Notes: Formalizes predictions that influence the outcomes/distributions they aim to predict.

Title: Algorithmic monoculture and social welfare
Notes: Under model assumptions, common reliance on a more accurate shared signal can worsen collective decision quality through correlated choices.

Title: Dissecting racial bias in an algorithm used to manage the health of populations
Author_or_Institution: Ziad Obermeyer; Brian Powers; Christine Vogeli; Sendhil Mullainathan
Notes: Shows a health-cost proxy can predict its chosen label while diverging from health need across groups.

Title: Administrative Burden: Learning, Psychological, and Compliance Costs in Citizen-State Interactions
Author_or_Institution: Donald Moynihan; Pamela Herd; Hope Harvey
Notes: Develops learning, psychological, and compliance costs as components of administrative burden.

Title: Magic Quadrant FAQ: How Markets and Vendors Are Evaluated in Gartner Magic Quadrants
Notes: States that client status does not affect inclusion/positioning and that Magic Quadrants should not be a buyer’s only vendor-selection tool.

Title: Correction to: how pervasive is corporate fraud?
Author_or_Institution: Alexander Dyck; Adair Morse; Luigi Zingales
Source_Type: peer-reviewed correction / Review of Accounting Studies
Notes: Correction addressing M-Score threshold, missing-value treatment, and a variable label; manuscript uses it to preserve adverse context around S112.
